synopsis: HIL tests production-controller timing, communications, interfaces and fault responses against a simulated plant; SIL cannot show whether the production processor misses deadlines [f5283, f529]. HIL requires deterministic hard real time because the real ECU cannot wait: missing even an expected 50-millisecond sensor-message deadline can produce a false test result, so throughput alone is insufficient [f13418, f16179, f13420]. Reported performance varies substantially: ISPRS 2024 terrain examples achieved 60 FPS for a single building and 17 FPS for a 23-million-Gaussian scene, while higher-fidelity Chrono CRM terrain reportedly runs 50–200 times slower than real time [f3893, f3894, f8499]. Sensor acceleration is promising but configuration-specific: 2020 vendor radar figures report about 12 ms per frame against a 30 FPS target, and a 2021 publication with vendor authors reports above 160 FPS for one single-channel radar [f4932, f4933]. Planning should therefore benchmark actual geometry, sensors, latency and jitter early, retaining separate offline high-fidelity and real-time models where necessary rather than assuming a generic real-time factor [f13425, f8924].
